Her long career has also earned major recognition, including the 2023 Curt Gowdy Electronic Media Award from the Basketball Hall of Fame.Arch Manning and Steve Sarkisian’s Holly Rowe moment takes another turnThe controversy began after Texas beat No. 1 Ohio State 24-23 on September 12. The Longhorns had fallen behind 23-3 before completing the comeback, with Manning helping lead the offense during the rally.After the game, Rowe tried to interview Sarkisian on the field. Instead of answering, he shouted, “Texas fight! Hook ’em!” and walked away to celebrate with his team. Rowe looked frustrated by the exchange.There was more context, however. ESPN’s Laura Rutledge explained that technical problems had already affected a halftime interview with Sarkisian. She said the coach had waited patiently and that ESPN owed him an apology. A Texas spokesperson later said technical problems happened again during the postgame interview.The AI video later changed the conversation. It falsely showed Sarkisian hitting Rowe. When Manning was asked about AI edits, he brought up that clip himself and said, “Of him slapping Holly Rowe? It’s hilarious.” His comments quickly drew criticism because the video showed violence against a woman, even though the scene was completely fake.For Rowe, the latest part of the story was not about the Texas win or Sarkisian’s interview. It was about Brunson choosing to defend her, and her simple response showed that the support meant something to her.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Capitals Say Alex Ovechkin Was Asked to Film United Russia Ad While Home This Summer
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — After NHL career goal-scoring leader Alex Ovechkin appeared in an ad for Vladimir Putin's United Russia party that came to light this week, the Washington Capitals said their long-time captain was asked to participate in the video campaign while back in his home country this summer.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — After NHL career goal-scoring leader Alex Ovechkin appeared in an ad for Vladimir Putin's United Russia party that came to light this week, the Washington Capitals said their long-time captain was asked to participate in the video campaign while back in his home country this summer.

"Alex Ovechkin is a Russian citizen who lives in Moscow with his family during the offseason and will live there following his retirement," team spokesperson Sergey Kocharov said Tuesday in a statement sent to The Associated Press. "As the longest-tenured athlete in Washington, D.C., and a pillar of the community, his focus and ours is on the season ahead and the continued impact he makes on the ice and in our city."

Ovechkin is seen in the commercial standing behind Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. Viacheslav "Slava" Fetisov also participated, leading to backlash on social media from fellow Hall of Famer Dominik Hasek, who called it support for Russia's war against Ukraine.

The NHL deferred to the Capitals when asked for comment. Ovechkin is expected to be made available to reporters on Thursday when training camp opens ahead of his 22nd NHL season.

Ovechkin, who turns 41 on Thursday, previously voiced support for the Russian president in 2017 when he started a social movement called the "Putin Team." At the time, he told reporters from the AP and The Washington Post, "I just support my country."

When Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, Ovechkin said, "Please, no more war," when asked about the situation. Asked then about his relationship with Putin, Ovechkin said: "He's my president, but I'm not in politics. I'm an athlete."

Putin has cracked down on dissent in the years since launching what he calls a special military operation in Ukraine, including punishment for referring to it as a war.

Ovechkin broke Wayne Gretzky's goals record in April 2024 with his 895th. He has scored 929 in his career, which began in 2005 after the Capitals took him with the first pick in the 2004 draft.

articles.title: Penta Reacts to Roman Reigns Loss, WWE Rumors on Seth Rollins, Stephanie Vaquer's Surprise Title Win
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Penta Vows to Become World Champ After Loss to Reigns

Lil Yachty Feels 'Like S--t' After WWE Debut

After falling short in his World Heavyweight Championship match against Roman Reigns during Monday night's episode of Raw in Mexico City, Penta insisted that fans have not seen the last of him in the WWE world title mix.

In a post-show promo posted on WWE's social media accounts, Penta said, "One day I will become a world heavyweight champion. I promise you."

Penta also expressed pride in his performance on Monday night, while giving Reigns his proverbial flowers, saying of The Tribal Chief, "I know now why he is one of the best in the world."

After winning a tournament to earn a world title match against Reigns, Penta finally got his shot Monday night on the first episode of Raw to take place in his home country of Mexico since 2011.

The crowd was firmly behind Penta, and he had The OTC on the ropes on numerous occasions. Reigns ultimately prevailed, but Penta proved he belonged in the ring with WWE's top dog.

It is apparent that WWE has a hugely popular star on its hands with Penta, so the challenge for the company now is to follow up on his performance in an effective way.

A world title win doesn't appear to be in his immediate future, but perhaps having him participate in and win the Money in the Bank ladder match would be the best way to keep him on the world title periphery, while making it clear that he is a champion in waiting.

Despite participating in WWE's live event loop in South America last week, Seth Rollins was reportedly never scheduled for Monday night's episode of Raw in Mexico.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), no backstage sources indicated that a Rollins appearance on Raw was in the cards, and it isn't yet clear what Rollins will do when he returns to WWE programming.

Most fans last saw Rollins at SummerSlam last month when he lost to Reigns in a World Heavyweight Championship match, which main evented Night 2.

Rollins has not been featured on any of WWE's weekly programming since then, and there hasn't been much mention of him either.

The Visionary finally resurfaced last week at a WWE house show in Quito, Ecuador, teaming with LA Knight and Solo Sikoa to beat The Usos and Jacob Fatu in a six-man tag team match.

Rollins worked multiple untelevised live events in South America, leading many to assume his televised return was imminent.

While that may ultimately prove to be true, it did not happen on Monday's episode of Raw, which was largely focused on Penta challenging Reigns for the world heavyweight title.

With Money in the Bank on the horizon next month, it could make sense for Rollins to return in the coming weeks and take part in a Money in the Bank qualifier given that he is a two-time Money in the Bank ladder match winner, including last year.

Reported Reason for Vaquer's Women's World Title Win

WWE surprised many on Saturday night when Stephanie Vaquer beat Liv Morgan for the Women's World Championship at a live event.

It turns out the reasoning behind the decision was quite simple, as WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Mrosko ) reported that WWE wanted to reward Vaquer with a big moment in her home country of Chile.

One night before the title change, it started to become apparent that it was possible since WWE was making a big deal of it on social media.

Most notably, Raw general manager Adam Pearce announced that Becky Lynch would serve as the special guest referee for the title match between Vaquer and Morgan in Chile.

Lynch ended up playing a huge role in the result, as she refused to count the three for Morgan after Liv attempted to cheat to win. That set the stage for Vaquer's massive victory in front of her home fans.

On Monday night's episode of Raw, WWE announced that those who sign up for the Club WWE subscription service will be able to watch the Vaquer vs. Morgan match in its entirety, giving fans extra incentive to sign up.

That match also set the stage for an entertaining opening segment and match on Raw in Mexico with Vaquer and new AAA mega champion El Grande Americano facing Morgan and Dominik Mysterio in a mixed tag team match.

articles.title: India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets to seal T20 series
articles.summary: Sanju Samson’s half century helps India seal three-match series with wins in first two games.
articles.body:
Sanju Samson scored 57 off 22 balls as India beat Afghanistan by seven wickets to clinch their three-match T20 series with a match to spare on Tuesday.

Samson hit four sixes and seven fours en route to his first half-century since this year’s T20 World Cup final – where he was named player of the tournament.

His opening partner Abhishek Sharma scored 39 off 19 balls – including four sixes – as the duo amassed 88 off only 38 balls.

India finished with 163-3 in 14.5 overs. It had won the first T20 by seven wickets as well, at the same venue on Sunday.

Afghanistan is playing host in this series, in a unique arrangement, and for the second game running, it finished with an under-par score after India won the toss and opted to field.

All-rounder Nitish Reddy picked 3-24 in three overs as Afghanistan was restricted to 159-8 in 20 overs.

Samson and Sharma set a hectic pace as India raced to 82-0 in the powerplay. Afghanistan used spin in the powerplay as compared to the first game, but to no avail.

Rashid Khan came on after the powerplay, getting the breakthrough in the seventh over, as Sharma was out caught at deep midwicket.

Samson carried on to reach his seventh T20 half-century off 20 balls. Khan picked a second wicket in the seventh over, as Samson holed out to long-off.

But India had powered its way to 100 in 7.1 overs – joint second-quickest for them since 2024.

Skipper Shreyas Iyer was Khan’s third victim, out caught at slip, but Ishan Kishan (38 not out) and Tilak Varma (15 not out) polished off the remaining runs without any bother.

Earlier, put in to bat, Afghanistan made another poor start. Rahmanullah Gurbaz fell for a second consecutive duck, this time to Arshdeep Singh.

Skipper Ibrahim Zadran scored 37 off 33 balls to make sure Afghanistan didn’t lose too many wickets in the powerplay again.

But the “hosts” slid from 59-2 to 100-6 in the middle overs and lost their base as Reddy picked two wickets. Afghanistan only managed to recover thanks to a 48-run partnership off 28 balls between Rashid Khan and Mohammad Nabi.

Khan hit 28 off 16 balls with three fours and a six, while Nabi scored 20 off 14 balls.

articles.title: Texas QB Arch Manning apologizes for ‘insensitive comment’ over AI video
articles.summary: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning apologized Tuesday for referencing an AI video of his head coach Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe in the wake of Texas’s win over Ohio State over the weekend.
articles.body: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning apologized Tuesday for referencing an AI video of his head coach Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe in the wake of Texas’s win over Ohio State over the weekend. On Saturday, Sarkisian first didn’t partake in a halftime interview with ESPN after reporter Laura Rutledge said the coach had to wait too long due to technical difficulties. Sarkisian was then approached by Rowe for a postgame interview, as is customary, but after yelling with excitement into the vicinity of Rowe, Sarkisian ran away before answering any questions. On Monday, Manning was asked by Inside Texas reporter Evan Vieth if he’d seen any social media videos about the Longhorns’ come-from-behind victory against the then-No. 1 Buckeyes, and Manning said he saw an AI video of Sarkisian striking Rowe. “I’ve seen a few AI edits of stuff but that’s about it. I saw an AI edit of Sark’s interview. Have you all seen that one? That’s a good one. Of him slapping Holly Rowe?” Manning said while laughing during a press conference. Vieth shared the video Monday, and it was met with swift backlash. On Tuesday, Manning apologized in an Instagram story. “In my press conference yesterday, I made an insensitive comment about an AI video. There is nothing funny about it,” Manning wrote. “It’s easy to say I didn’t mean it, but I know my words and actions were hurtful to a lot of people. I do not that that lightly and am deeply sorry for that.” Manning added: “I specifically want to apologize to Holly Rowe for what she has personally had to deal with because of my comments. I have a ton of respect for her and appreciate her showing me grace in this moment. I need to do better and will be more thoughtful going forward.” Vieth, who initially described Manning’s response as “gold,” also apologized Monday. “I sincerely apologize for how I chose to present the tweet, and I’ll be more careful going forward,” he wrote in part of a social media post. Rowe thanked Manning for his apology on Tuesday. “I appreciate our conversation about this which will remain private. Apology accepted,” she wrote on social media. “We move forward with respect and kindness for one another.” Manning, 22, is in his senior season at Texas. The nephew of NFL legends Peyton Manning and Eli Manning, he was a consensus five-star recruit before committing to the Longhorns in December 2022. He is also a highly regarded NFL prospect, and is widely expected to be a first-round pick in next year’s draft. He is seeking to be the third generation of the Manning family to play in the NFL after Peyton, Eli and his grandfather Archie. Rowe, 60, has worked full time at ESPN since 1998. She is a reporter on several major events, including college football, the WNBA, and the women’s NCAA Final Four. In 2023, Rowe received the Curt Gowdy Electronic Media Award from the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. She is also an advocate for cancer research after she was diagnosed with metastatic melanoma in 2015.

articles.title: Texas rallied late to beat Ohio State in a great game. Why people are talking about an AI video and a Texas candidate instead
articles.summary: Julian Sayin’s last-second heave bounced around, the ball eventually landing in the hands of Texas’ Graceson Littleton, sealing the Longhorns’ incredible comeback over No. 1 Ohio State on Saturday.
articles.body: Julian Sayin’s last-second heave bounced around, the ball eventually landing in the hands of Texas’ Graceson Littleton, sealing the Longhorns’ incredible comeback over No. 1 Ohio State on Saturday. It was a moment of pure joy. The burnt-orange clad players rushed the field, star quarterback Arch Manning looking wild with glee as he sprinted around the field holding up the school’s signature “hook ‘em” hand gesture. Since that moment, little time has been spent talking about the actual game played on the field, thanks to a fired-up Steve Sarkisian blowing off a post-game interview, a little-known Texas politician making racist comments about the school’s student body and then Manning (and a room full of much older reporters and other individuals) laughing about an AI video depicting violence against ESPN reporter Holly Rowe. The conversation surrounding the Longhorns this week was expected to center on their playoff chances, Manning living up to sky-high expectations and Sarkisian finally breaking through and completing an incredible comeback from the personal troubles that plagued his time at Washington and USC. The vibes should be great in Austin. Instead, the discourse centers about concerns about misogyny in the football program and the racial makeup of the student body – something no one would have predicted in those gleeful moments late Saturday night. It all started just seconds after the final moments ticked away when ESPN’s Holly Rowe began to ask Sarkisian a question on the field at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. The Texas head coach had abandoned a halftime on-field interview with Laura Rutledge, which the sideline reporter chalked up to technical difficulties that cut into the coach’s limited halftime intermission. As Rowe began to speak, an amped-up Sarkisian leaned toward the microphone and yelled, “That’s called Texas fight! That’s called Texas fight! Hook ‘em!” and walked away. Rowe looked frustrated for a moment before walking out of frame, while Sarkisian went to celebrate with the team. It was a contentious moment clearly fueled by adrenaline and a desire to be with his players, something that wasn’t the best look but was easily understandable. After an incredible fourth-quarter comeback (the Longhorns trailed 23-3 when the quarter started and won 24-23), Sarkisian wanted to spend his time with his players, not ESPN. Fair enough. Arch Manning steps in it But with social media being the AI-filled cesspool that it is, some people took that moment and decided to run with it in gross ways. One such AI-generated video showed Sarkisian’s interaction with Rowe, but edited in a virtual Sarkisian rearing back and striking a virtual Rowe across the face while shouting, “Hook ‘em!” before running away. It is the kind of shameful content that strange people on the internet decide to create because they think it’s funny, without considering the fact they are using images of real people who have real lives and real emotions and using those images to create something abhorrent. Social media has already allowed many users to hide behind their keyboards to say (or create) things they would never dream of if they had to interact with their targets in real-world situations, all under the guise of “it’s just a joke.” And for people like Manning, a 22-year-old who has never known a time without social media or the culture around it, it might all feel normal. Manning was asked on Monday if he had seen any of AI-generated videos of the postgame celebrations. Reporter Evan Vieth asked the question, explaining later – in a post apologizing for referring to Manning’s answer as “gold” – that he had asked about AI-generated videos of Manning’s joyous run around the turf after the final seconds ran out. “I’ve seen a few AI edits of stuff but that’s about it. I saw an AI edit of Sark’s interview,” Manning said with a smile, using his coach’s nickname, looking to his right at someone off-screen – something he’d do a couple times in the next few seconds. That brought a round of laughter from the room in which his press conference was being held. “Have y’all seen that one?” Manning asked the room. “That’s a good one. Of him slapping Holly Rowe?” That brought another round of laughter, though softer than the first. Manning added, “That’s hilarious.” It’s really not, even in the shock-and-awe world of social media where AI has let users create increasingly absurd images and videos in the infinite search for online clout, whatever that’s worth. Manning’s comments were crass and ill-thought, a brief look into the psyche of the average college-aged athlete who sees shocking images online and chooses to laugh at them as a joke rather than consider the bigger picture. On Tuesday afternoon, he issued an apology on Instagram. “In my press conference yesterday, I made an insensitive comment about an AI video. There is nothing funny about it. It’s easy to say I didn’t mean it, but I know my words and actions were hurtful to a lot of people. I do not take that lightly and am deeply sorry for that,” he wrote. “I specifically want to apologize to Holly Rowe for what she has personally had to deal with because of my comments. I have a ton of respect for her and appreciate her showing me grace in this moment. I need to do better and will be more thoughtful going forward.” Later on Tuesday, Rowe posted a reply to Manning’s mea culpa on Instagram and X. “Thank you, Arch. I appreciate our conversation about this — which will remain private. “Apology accepted. We move forward with respect and kindness for one another.” ESPN declined to comment on Manning’s press conference. Not being thoughtful isn’t a crime and everyone has said something they later come to regret. For Manning, it’s a moment that he will likely cringe at going forward and hope to learn from as he becomes a bigger star. What is more disturbing is the laughter in the room after Manning mentioned the video showed Sarkisian “slapping Holly Rowe.” Vieth’s video didn’t show who was cracking up at the idea, but – generally speaking – the older and more mature people in the room should know better. Texas’ student body targeted There is another, wholly separate distraction from Saturday night’s victory that has dragged the national immigration debate and culture wars directly into the grandstands at Memorial Stadium. The official account of the Texas athletic department posted a video late on Saturday showing the student section absolutely losing their minds as Texas scored the tying touchdown, which would be followed by the game-winning extra point. It’s the kind of scene that highlights why people love sports: delirious joy, screaming, students jumping up and down and hugging each other – a community brought together to cheer on their team. It was a beautiful sight for basically everyone who didn’t attend Oklahoma or Texas A&M, the Longhorns’ traditional rivals. Unless you are Bo French. French, who is running for Texas Railroad Commissioner (a body that, despite its name, oversees oil and gas regulation in the state), noticed that many of the students in that particular video were people of color. “I heard UT graduation this year looked like this. I didn’t believe it. The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined,” he wrote, replying to the video on X on Sunday morning. He later added: “Like body-cams exposed criminals, social media is exposing how many Americans have been displaced by foreigners. It’s everywhere and far worse than any of us could imagine.” French, of course, has no way of knowing how many of those students are from another country or are from Texas. Given that the student body of UT-Austin is about 90% made up of students from the Lone Star State, it’s overwhelmingly likely that the students in that video are Texans – regardless of their skin color. It’s unclear what role a prospective Texas Railroad Commissioner believes he should play regarding the demographic makeup of the state’s flagship university, but a quick scroll of French’s X feed reveals extensive commentary on foreigners and people of color, with relatively few mentions of the oil and gas industry that he says he’s running to support. Lifelong Texans, who just happen to have a different skin color than French, now have to grapple with being made to feel like outsiders in a community that is meant to stay with them for life. The student newspaper at UT-Austin, The Daily Texan, spoke with several students who now feel separate from the community that has become part of their identity. The impact on campus has been tangible and disheartening. In a period of American history when our politics have grown increasingly caustic and embroiled in culture wars meant to sow divisions along so many different demographic lines that it’s hard to keep track, sports remain a rare unifier. The video French responded to captured a beautiful and genuine human moment: people of all colors and backgrounds coming together to celebrate and feel the pure joy that sports can bring. The Longhorns line up against UT-San Antonio on Saturday night for their next game, their first as No. 1 since early last season. That moment, and the unity that comes when the ball is kicked off, cannot come soon enough.

articles.title: Peterborough beat Barnsley on penalties on EFL Cup
articles.summary: Peterborough move into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup thanks to a 7-6 penalty shootout victory over Barnsley that followed a thrilling 3-3 draw between...
articles.body:
Peterborough United 3 - 3 Barnsley AET (7 - 6)

Peterborough moved into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2009 thanks to a 7-6 penalty shootout victory over Barnsley that followed a thrilling 3-3 draw between the two League One sides.

Barnsley were gifted the lead after 61 seconds when Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass was charged down by Cameron McGeehan , with the Tykes captain nodding in after the ball had come off the bar.

Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca's cross was pushed out by Barnsley goalkeeper Kieran Flavell as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in.

The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills' free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod.

But the Tykes were level five minutes before half-time when Reyes Cleary beat Mendonca with ease down the left before placing his shot into the bottom corner.

The visitors looked to have won it when Cleary bent in his second in the 74th minute, but Ormerod sent the tie to penalties by heading in Mills' cross with just two minutes remaining.

After 12 successful spot-kicks, a tame effort from Barnsley's Luke Alker was saved by Bass, giving Harrison Jones the chance to send the hosts through, which he did.

articles.title: Coleraine strike late to break Glentoran hearts
articles.summary: Substitute Lewis McGregor fired home the winner in the final seconds of the game to seal a dramatic 2-1 win for Coleraine over Glentoran at the Oval.
articles.body:
Substitute Lewis McGregor fired home the winner in the final seconds of the game to seal a dramatic 2-1 win for Coleraine over Glentoran at the Oval.

The game appeared to be heading for a 1-1 draw before McGregor pounced deep in added time to extend the league leaders' unbeaten run to 14 games.

Earlier, Joe Thomson had broken the deadlock against his former employers after he came off the bench, while fellow substitute, Jordan Jenkins, equalised for the home side with less than 10 minutes remaining.

It was a disappointing end to a game for the home side who held their own against the league leaders despite a turbulent start to the week following manager Declan Devine's departure on Monday.

Coleraine extend unbeaten run with win over Glens

Coleraine settled early and created a number of good chances inside the opening quarter.

First, Matthew Shevlin raced on to a long ball out of defence from Ben Doherty before testing Glentoran goalkeeper Billy Crellin with a crisp shot from 12 yards.

Moments later Will Patching and Jay Henderson combined to create an opening for Joel Cooper but the former Linfield man's volley went the wrong side of the crossbar.

And Shevlin really should have done better when again presented with another opportunity by the impressive Doherty, the unmarked striker lifting his shot over the crossbar from six yards out.

Glentoran, too, had their chances, forcing Coleraine goalkeeper Lewis Webb into a number of fine saves in an entertaining first half.

First, he dived acrobatically low to his left to block Greg Sloggett's volley from distance before getting down low at his near post to divert Jordan Stewart's low drive away for a corner.

Ross Clarke's strength saw him outmuscle Ben Doherty but no one in a Glentoran could get on the end of his inviting ball across the face of goal.

The visitors again were on the front foot in the early stages of the second half and Joel Cooper twice went close.

First, he was denied at close range by a smart stop from Crellin who raced quickly off his line before a snapshot curled wide of the far post after Will Patching's free-kick had been blocked.

The visitors broke the deadlock with just under 20 minutes remaining thanks to second-half sub Thomson.

The former Glentoran man, on the pitch only a matter of minutes, was quickest to react when the ball fell to him after Matthew Shevlin had challenged Billy Crellin to a Ben Doherty cross, drilling a low shot past a number of covering defenders.

The Glens weren't behind for long as substitute Jenkins levelled with seven minutes remaining, capitalising on some hesitant Coleraine defending to nip in and force the ball over the line from eight yards.

But there was still more drama to come as yet another sub - McGregor - reacted quickest to a loose ball inside the Glentoran penalty area to sweep home what proved to be the winner deep into added time.

articles.title: Detroit Lions Add Defensive Starter to Week 2 Injury Report
articles.summary: The Lions added starting CB D.J. Reed to their Week 2 injury report Tuesday, while three starting offensive linemen remain limited or out.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions ' Week 2 injury report picked up a significant new name Tuesday.

Starting cornerback D.J. Reed was added with a foot injury and was listed as a limited participant as Detroit continued preparations for Thursday night's matchup with the Buffalo Bills .

Reed was not listed Monday, making his addition the biggest change from the Lions' initial report. The veteran cornerback started Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over New Orleans and finished with 10 tackles and a pass breakup.

That would be worth monitoring during any week.

Four days before facing Josh Allen , after Detroit just allowed Tyler Shough to throw for 410 yards?

Detroit conducted another walkthrough Tuesday, so all participation levels are estimates rather than results from a full practice. The Lions' official Sept. 15 practice report lists five players.

NP: Did Not Participate LP: Limited Participation FP: Full Participation

*The Lions conducted walkthroughs Monday and Tuesday. Participation designations are estimates.

Lions Offensive Line Remains the Bigger Problem

Reed is the new concern. Detroit's offensive line remains the existing one.

Christian Mahogany and Blake Miller were again listed as non-participants, while center Juice Scruggs remained limited. That means the same three starting offensive linemen who appeared on Detroit's initial Week 2 injury report are still dealing with issues two days before kickoff.

Mahogany's status appears particularly shaky. Dan Campbell said Monday that he does not expect the hip injury to become a serious long-term problem, but acknowledged that getting him ready for Thursday could be difficult. We broke down Campbell's latest Mahogany update here .

Miller's continued absence is also worth watching after the rookie started at right tackle against New Orleans.

Christian Izien was listed as a full participant for the second consecutive day after missing Week 1 with a groin injury. His return would be welcome for a secondary that now has Reed dealing with a foot issue.

Wednesday Becomes Important Before Lions-Bills

Detroit's final report Wednesday should provide a much clearer picture.

The Lions and Bills kick off Thursday at 8:15 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium , with both teams entering 1-0 after narrow Week 1 victories. Buffalo's official Week 2 preview

The biggest questions remain along Detroit's offensive line.

But Reed's appearance Tuesday added another one in a hurry.

Against Josh Allen, that is not exactly the position group where Detroit wanted a fresh injury concern.

articles.title: Commanders’ safety Tyler Owens is the first ‘Angry Runs’ winner of 2026
articles.summary: Tyler Owens continues to receive praise for his awesome work on special teams.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders safety Tyler Owens made himself a household name during Sunday's season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles . The 6-foot-2, 213-pound third-year safety went viral for a special-teams rep, plowing through two Eagles on his way downfield and bodyslamming Philadelphia's punt returner.

NFL legends and others have praised the play, saying coaches at all levels should use the play as teaching tape. Not only technique, but hustle, too.

On Tuesday, in the 2026 debut of "Angry Runs," Kyle Brandt of "Good Morning Football" picked Owens as the winner, becoming only the third defensive player in the award's history and the first on special teams to win a scepter.

In picking Owens, Brandt called it the "greatest thing" he's ever seen on "Angry Runs." He called it the greatest thing he's ever seen in life and football. "Unbelievable," he said.

After Brandt named Owens the winner, he joined "Good Morning Football." Owens said he was actually angry on the play.

"Angry Runs" began back in 2017, and Ravens running back Derrick Henry has won the most scepters. Owens is only the second Washington player to win the award, joining Austin Ekeler , who won in 2024.

articles.title: Reading 1 Brentford 2: Carvalho marks comeback with goal as Bees progress to Carabao Cup round four
articles.summary: Fábio Carvalho marked his first competitive appearance in 318 days with a goal as Brentford defeated Reading 2-1 to progress to round four of the Carabao Cup...
articles.body:
Fábio Carvalho marked his first competitive appearance in 318 days with a goal as Brentford defeated Reading 2-1 to progress to round four of the Carabao Cup.

Callum Wilson opened the scoring inside three minutes before Carvalho doubled the Bees' advantage in first-half stoppage time. Paudie O'Connor pulled one back for Reading after the break, but Keith Andrews' side held firm at Select Car Leasing Stadium.

The Bees boss made eight changes to his starting XI. Among those coming into the side was Carvalho , who was involved in a competitive fixture for the first time since Brentford's trip to Crystal Palace on 1 November 2025.

The midfielder was subsequently sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament injury before returning to action with the B team and featuring for the first team against Rennes in pre-season.

Goalkeeper Ellery Balcombe made his second senior appearance for the club, while summer signing El Hadji Malick Diouf started for the first time .

Brentford took the lead inside three minutes. Carvalho fed Dango Ouattara down the right and, when he slipped while attempting to collect the return pass, the ball ran through to Wilson . The striker swept a composed finish into the bottom corner from 12 yards.

Rico Henry , partnering Kristoffer Ajer in central defence, made an important intervention, cutting out Josh Stokes' through ball before Randell Williams could latch on to it.

The Royals had the ball in the net on 12 minutes through Paudie O'Connor's acrobatic finish, but the referee ruled it out for a high foot.

O'Connor then headed Charlie Savage 's free-kick from the left onto the roof of the net, while Diouf's long-range effort at the opposite end flew over the crossbar.

Midway through the half, Randell Williams worked the ball into the box and Balcombe made a sprawling save to deny Jamie Reid.

Reading kept the attack alive. Williams' deflected cross travelled towards the back post, where Reid slipped as he attempted to meet it, and the ball bounced behind for a goal-kick.

Damsgaard 's cross from the right was flicked on by Wilson and Keane Lewis-Potter met it with a fierce strike, forcing Joel Pereira to launch himself to his right and push the ball behind for a corner.

Diouf sent the ball up the channel and O'Connor's slip presented Wilson with a sight of goal, but the striker could not generate enough power to trouble Pereira, who gathered his shot comfortably.

Lewis-Potter then teed up Carvalho on the edge of the box, but his shot was blocked by a Reading defender.

Henry produced another vital intervention on 45 minutes, racing back to poke the ball away from Reid as the forward closed in on goal. From the resulting corner, Conor Masterson glanced Savage's in-swinging delivery narrowly wide .

Brentford doubled their lead in the final seconds before the break. Ouattara played a defence-splitting pass that Wilson cleverly dummied, allowing the ball to run into Carvalho's path. The midfielder took a touch to set himself before calmly slotting home.

Shortly after the restart, Brentford moved the ball from left to right across the face of Reading's penalty area. Ouattara received a pass from Wilson and drove narrowly wide from 10 yards.

Balcombe got down quickly to smother Josh Stokes' shot after the ball broke to him in the Bees' box.

Andrews' side came close to adding a third on 63 minutes. Henry clipped a first-time cross towards the back post, where Ouattara's header was clawed away by Pereira. Kayode then fired into the side netting from close range.

Ouattara then threatened again, heading Kayode's cross just over the bar.

Reading reduced the deficit on 72 minutes. Ajer bravely blocked Stokes' goal bound effort, but O'Connor nodded home from Savage's resulting corner.

Kayode's cross bounced through to substitute Igor Thiago as the Bees looked to restore their two-goal advantage, but the striker failed to make clean contact and Pereira gathered comfortably.

Thiago turned provider moments later, teeing up Damsgaard on the edge of the box, but the Dane skewed his effort high and wide.

Thiago latched on to Lewis-Potter's ball over the top and held off Jeriel Dorsett , but Pereira raced off his line to narrow the angle and deny the striker.

Jannik Schuster headed in a corner in the final seconds, but the referee disallowed the goal for a foul.

Brentford will find out their next Carabao Cup opponents following the conclusion of the televised tie between Manchester United and Brighton and Hove Albion on Wednesday night.

Reading: Pereira; Ahmed, Masterson, O'Connor (Dorsett 79), Roberts (Lane 63); Savage, Fraser; Williams, Stokes (Earthy 88), Kyerewaa (Lisbie 79); Reid (Brown 63)

Subs: Stevens, Godwin-Malife, Wing, Beacroft

Brentford: Balcombe; Kayode, Ajer, Henry, Diouf (Schuster 61); Ouattara (Anthony 77), Damsgaard, Sangaré (Yarmoliuk HT), Lewis-Potter; Carvalho (Hickey 77), Wilson (Thiago 77)

Subs: Kelleher , Fredrick, Janelt, Schade

articles.title: Joey Loperfido back with Houston Astros as Taylor Trammell goes on paternity list
articles.summary: Joey Loperfido is returning to the majors after being demoted to Triple-A two months ago.
articles.body:
The Houston Astros placed outfielder Taylor Trammell on the paternity list and recalled outfielder Joey Loperfido from Triple-A Sugar Land prior to Tuesday's series opener against the Kansas City Royals .

A player can spend up to three days on Major League Baseball's paternity list.

Trammell has played in 91 games for the Astros this season, posting a .204/.292/.353 slash line and 82 OPS-plus. He had started 10 of the team's last 12 games before Tuesday, mostly in left field.

Loperfido, the Astros' opening day left fielder, has a .216/.314/.333 slash line and 84 OPS-plus over 39 major-league games this season. He was optioned to the minors in early July and is batting .289 with a .766 OPS in 58 games for Triple-A Sugar Land.

articles.title: Liverpool 3-1 Tottenham: Mac Allister, Gakpo and Szoboszlai Fire Reds Through in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Liverpool booked their place in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with a 3-1 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Anfield, as Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo...
articles.body:
Liverpool booked their place in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with a 3-1 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Anfield, as Alexis Mac Allister , Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai delivered the decisive moments on an encouraging night for Andoni Iraola 's much-changed side.

Mac Allister opened the scoring with an excellent first-half finish before Gakpo doubled Liverpool's advantage shortly after the interval. Conor Gallagher threatened to make the closing stages uncomfortable when he pulled one back for Tottenham, but Giorgi Mamardashvili produced a crucial late save before Szoboszlai settled the tie spectacularly with a thunderous long-range strike.

It was not always comfortable, particularly during Tottenham's late push for an equaliser, but Liverpool ultimately had enough quality when it mattered.

Mac Allister Gives Liverpool the Breakthrough

With Iraola making 10 changes to his starting XI, there was always likely to be a slightly different rhythm to Liverpool's performance.

Tottenham had opportunities of their own during an open start, with Lucas Bergvall denied by Mamardashvili, while Lewis Koumas forced Martin Dubravka into action at the opposite end.

The breakthrough arrived after 21 minutes and came from one of Liverpool's most experienced players.

Mac Allister found himself in space around the Tottenham penalty area and produced a superb finish into the top corner, giving Dubravka little chance and handing Liverpool a 1-0 advantage.

It was exactly the kind of contribution Liverpool needed from the Argentine.

After scoring against Atletico Madrid last week, Mac Allister has now found the net in successive appearances and looks increasingly confident under Iraola.

His willingness to attack the penalty area was particularly noticeable. Mac Allister has always possessed the technical quality to contribute goals from midfield, and his latest finish was another reminder of just how dangerous he can be when given licence to push forward.

Speaking after the match, he also highlighted the importance of the support he has received from the Liverpool crowd and the responsibility experienced players have towards the club's younger players.

On a night when several youngsters were handed an opportunity, Mac Allister led by example.

Liverpool emerged after half-time determined to take greater control of the tie and quickly extended their advantage through Gakpo.

The Dutch international struck shortly after the restart, firing Liverpool into a 2-0 lead and putting Iraola's side firmly in command.

Gakpo's latest contribution continues an impressive opening to the season.

He now has two goals and three assists from five appearances, numbers which underline his growing influence within the Liverpool attack.

There had been considerable speculation surrounding Gakpo during the transfer window, but his recent performances have demonstrated why keeping him at Anfield could prove important.

His versatility remains a major asset. Whether operating from the left, centrally or moving between positions during matches, Gakpo offers Liverpool a combination of physical strength, intelligent movement and finishing ability.

Against Tottenham, he again delivered when the opportunity arrived.

Liverpool Youngsters Take Their Opportunity

The Carabao Cup has traditionally provided Liverpool with an opportunity to give younger players meaningful first-team minutes, and Iraola continued that approach against Spurs.

Making 10 changes inevitably brought an element of risk, particularly against Premier League opposition, but there were plenty of positives in Liverpool's performance.

Mac Allister praised the youngsters afterwards, explaining that their attitude in training has impressed the senior players.

He said they "show every day in training they want to be here" and predicted that they could become "really, really important" during the season.

Liverpool have a demanding campaign ahead and squad depth will inevitably be tested. Cup competitions provide valuable minutes for players on the fringes, but performances such as this can also give Iraola greater confidence about using younger players in Premier League matches when necessary.

There will be tougher tests ahead, but progressing while resting the majority of the first-choice XI represents a useful outcome.

At 2-0, Liverpool appeared to be cruising towards the fourth round.

Tottenham, however, refused to disappear.

Gallagher headed home shortly before the 70-minute mark to reduce the deficit to 2-1 and suddenly Liverpool found themselves under genuine pressure.

Spurs pushed numbers forward and forced Liverpool deeper during the closing stages, creating the kind of frantic finish Iraola would probably have preferred to avoid.

Mamardashvili then produced arguably one of the most important moments of the night.

With Tottenham searching for an equaliser, the Liverpool goalkeeper made an outstanding late save to preserve the advantage.

Liverpool have considerable competition in goal, but nights like this offer Mamardashvili the opportunity to demonstrate his quality. The save ensured Tottenham never completed their comeback and allowed Liverpool to deliver the final blow moments later.

If there was any lingering doubt about the outcome, Szoboszlai removed it in extraordinary fashion.

With the game entering its final moments, the Hungarian unleashed a ferocious volley from around 30 yards which flew beyond Dubravka.

It was a spectacular way to complete the scoring.

Liverpool had been forced to withstand significant Tottenham pressure after Gallagher's goal, but Szoboszlai's strike transformed a potentially nervous conclusion into a convincing-looking 3-1 victory.

Sometimes cup ties require exactly that kind of moment.

Liverpool had not dominated every phase of the contest, nor had they completely shut Tottenham down. What they did possess, however, was greater quality in the decisive moments.

Mac Allister found the top corner. Gakpo punished Tottenham after the restart. Mamardashvili produced a vital save. Szoboszlai then delivered the spectacular finish.

The Carabao Cup may not sit at the top of Liverpool's priorities this season, but this still felt like a useful victory.

Iraola was able to rotate heavily, give minutes to younger members of his squad and rest several regular starters ahead of the return to Premier League action.

There are still areas requiring improvement. Tottenham created enough opportunities to make the contest uncomfortable and Liverpool briefly surrendered control after establishing a two-goal advantage.

But cup football is ultimately about surviving and advancing.

Mac Allister continues to rediscover his influence, Gakpo remains productive, Mamardashvili delivered when required and Szoboszlai supplied a spectacular final flourish.

A 3-1 victory, another place in the Carabao Cup draw and valuable minutes throughout the squad.

For Iraola, it was a night with considerably more positives than negatives.

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur 1-3 Liverpool: Spurs unlucky to drop from League Cup
articles.summary: Lots of positives despite the result.
articles.body:
When the season kicked off, there would have been hope that Tottenham Hotspur could make a decent fist of things in the cup competitions, with a reasonably deep squad and limited fixture congestion with no European football. Those hopes were dashed with regards to the EFL Cup as Spurs visited one of their graveyards in the form of Anfield, as they went down 3-1 to Liverpool in an exciting and hard-fought match.

There was heavy rotation from both sides, with both Roberto De Zerbi and Andoni Iraola already conscious of the potential for injury to players; De Zerbi especially so given Spurs' recent history. De Zerbi made eight changes to his XI from the goalless draw against Everton , while Iraola made ten following Liverpool's matching scoreline against Fulham .

The volume of changes briefly appeared to manifest as a lack of cohesion and quality for both sides, with neither initially able to string multiple passes together, but Spurs were the side to adjust earliest. They were soon on the front foot, culminating in a massive early chance for Lucas Bergvall . Conor Gallagher played a well-placed through ball to the path of Destiny Udogie down the left, whose square ball found the late run of the Swede, who had ghosted in towards the penalty spot. A goal looked guaranteed but for the outstretched leg of Giorgi Mamardashvili , who somehow pulled off a save despite diving the wrong way.

Liverpool soon had a chance of their own, as Rio Ngumoha fed a pass through to Lewis Koumas , who ran off the back of Marcos Senesi . His attempt was saved by Martin Dubravka , but Ngumoha was soon involved again as Liverpool opened the scoring. Ngumoha dribbled at Udogie, with a piece of bad luck as the Italian stuck a foot in to make a tackle causing the ball to squirt out in Alexis Mac Allister 's direction. The Argentine struck it first time from the top of the box and Dubravka was left stranded as the ball sailed into the top right corner.

Further chances followed for both sides: Mohammed Kudus could have done better with an Udogie square ball, skying his attempt, while MacAllister could have doubled the lead after Spurs gave the ball away in their own half and Koumas cut the ball after receiving the ball from James McConnell . Despite the numerous chances, though, there remained a solitary goal in the cup tie with Liverpool taking their lead into the half.

It didn't take long for Liverpool to increase their lead in the second stanza with the simplest of goals. The ball found its way to Cody Gakpo on Liverpool's left, and he took one touch to create the smallest amount of space between him and Archie Gray before striking the ball firmly into the side netting with Dubravka once more unable to do much about the goal.

Changes for both sides followed as Spurs kept pushing for a goal. A mazy run by Omar Marmoush should have resulted in more, as the ball fell to Kudus who shot with Mamardashvili saving, but with nobody on hand to knock home the rebound. Marmoush should have done better with a chance of his own when fed by Bergvall, but took an extra touch and went down under contact. On replay, it could have potentially been a penalty, but instead once more Spurs walked away from a dangerous attack with nothing.

That soon changed though as Spurs opened their account with a goal from Gallagher. It was an excellent delivery by Mateus Fernandes on a corner kick, with the ball dipping over the outstretched arms of Mamardashvili, who had been smartly blocked off by Senesi. It was a simple headed finish by Gallagher, with Spurs back in the match with the score at 2-1.

Spurs were heavily on the front foot, but Liverpool still had chances of their own, with one coming thanks to a poor Tosin Adarabioyo giveaway just outside his own penalty area. The ball came to substitute Dominik Szoboszlai who wasted the chance, shooting straight at Dubravka. Spurs continued to be similarly profligate: A deflected Marmoush shot looked like it would sneak in, but Mamardashvili reacted brilliantly to palm the ball over; and Savio beat Milos Kerkez easily before dragging a shot wide.

It momentarily looked like Spurs could find the equalizer, but all their effort was for naught as Szoboszlai struck a killer blow with a sumptuous strike. The ball bounced out to the Hungarian around 30 yards out, as he volleyed a rocket of a strike into the top corner and secure the 3-1 result for Liverpool.

Hey, Spurs scored a goal, and against a Premier League opponent!

Look, the result is disappointing, but there are a lot of positives to take from this in what was probably Spurs' best performance of the season.

Would it even be reasonable to say that Spurs got #football'd? xG was 1.53 to 2.34 to Spurs, with Spurs creating three big chances to Liverpool's two, but the ball just wouldn't go in the net for the Lilywhites, while Liverpool were just lethal with some unbelievable finishes.

Lucas Bergvall had probably one of his best performances of the season, and part of that was being paired with Bentancur in the first half and Fernandes after the Uruguayan was subbed off. He looked a million times more comfortable as the more dynamic role in the double pivot, as opposed to when he's played alongside Sandro Tonali with that matchup just not really working.

Another who has looked to have taken a step up this season is Archie Gray. He's not a right back, and it's hard to blame him too much for Gakpo's goal, but the pseudo-inverted role he played in this match suited him well, with some excellent runs and good passing into space. He's getting better and better.

That was a nasty piece of contact from Cody Gakpo on Rodrigo Bentancur early in the second half. It was clearly unintentional, but one of those follow-throughs that VAR might have been tempted to look at, if VAR had been available, similar to Marmoush going down; was he clipped without a touch on the ball?

I'm not sure it's going to work for Mathys Tel at Spurs. The guy is fast, and strikes the ball well… but every time possession comes out to the young Frenchman play just completely stops. He has very little awareness of his teammates or the defense, and that sort of game intelligence isn't something that just appears out of nowhere. I really want it to work for him, but it's getting harder to say it will.

Fernandes HAS to play in central midfield. He was fantastic after coming on, and Spurs went up another level thanks in large part to his passing. In fact, all of Spurs' best performances so far this season have been with him in the double pivot.

Look, it's disappointing, but it's just one of those games. Regardless of the result, it was a strong performance and De Zerbi will be hoping the team can build on that against a struggling Aston Villa side this weekend.

articles.title: Liverpool v Tottenham player ratings from Carabao Cup as youngsters shine but Spurs stars flop
articles.summary: Liverpool 3-1 Tottenham: Spurs named a strong side but could not get their first win of the season as they exited the Carabao Cup
articles.body:
A much-changed Liverpool side knocked Tottenham out of the Carabao Cup to continue their winless start to the season under Roberto De Zerbi .

Spurs named a strong team, started well and should have taken a first-half lead when a cross fell to the feet of Lucas Bergvall in the box, but goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili made a stunning stop to deny him.

Liverpool then almost cut through Spurs as Rio Ngumoha found Lewis Koumas , only to be denied by Martin Dubravka , before Alexis Mac Allister fired the opening goal with a first-time shot into the top corner from the edge of the box.

Tottenham had not come from behind to win in 47 previous attempts and their task became even harder when Cody Gakpo cut inside from the left and slammed Liverpool into a two-goal lead shortly after the break.

Conor Gallagher belatedly scored Tottenham's first goal of the season to set up a frantic ending, but Dominik Szoboszlai 's late rocket sent Liverpool through to the fourth round.

Here are how the players rated at Anfield

Giorgi Mamardashvili, 8: Liverpool's No 2 goalkeeper made an excellent early stop to deny Lucas Bergvall when the tie was goalless, and another from Omar Marmoush later on. But he looked weak from the corner that led to Tottenham's goal.

Jeremie Frimpong , 5: Both of Tottenham's big first-half chances came down his side while, in an attacking sense, his final ball from the right was poor once again. But stuck to his task against the lively Mathys Tel .

Ronald Araujo , 7: The only player to keep his place from Saturday's 0-0 draw with Fulham . He displayed authority in the backline in another promising display from the on-loan Barcelona centre-back.

Joe Gomez , 6: Perhaps some rust would have been expected as the injury-prone defender made his first start of the season, but he slotted in well enough and had a role in Mac Allister's goal.

Milos Kerkez , 6: Solid enough defensively, with some bright bursts going forward too. An excellent recovery challenge to deny Omar Marmoush in the box was his highlight.

Alexis Mac Allister , 8: Delivered another big Anfield goal on a night where Liverpool needed his experience and he showed up. Showed his class at times.

Trey Nyoni , 7: Deployed in the deep-lying midfield position, the 19-year-old didn't put a foot wrong once he had adjusted to the pace of the game and Tottenham's fast start.

Rio Ngumoha, 7: Produced a wonderful turn and pass to set up an early chance for Lewis Koumas and also had a hand in Mac Allister's opener. The 18-year-old continues to adjust to the right side of attack.

James McConnell , 7: A very bright showing, full of energy, and led the hugely improved Liverpool press that rather set the tone for the night. Like Nyoni, didn't look out of place

Cody Gakpo , 8: Continued his superb start to the season with a trademark finish while coming inside onto his right foot. Brought incision to Liverpool's attack and scored while wearing the armband, too.

Lewis Koumas, 7: Didn't stop running all night and worked his socks off, despite playing in an unfamiliar position. Had an excellent chance to open the scoring after making a peeling run but was denied by Dubravka.

Jeremy Jacquet , 7: Made an excellent recovery challenge on Marmoush in the second half.

Ryan Gravenberch , 6: Liverpool actually lost some control after he replaced Nyoni.

Dominik Szoboszlai , 7: Wowzer. What a way to seal victory - and after wasting a late chance to put the game to bed.

Bradley Barcola , N/A: Showed some electric pace on the counter-attack, but Frimpong couldn't find him.

Alexander Isak , N/A: Led a very late breakaway but could not find the target.

Martin Dubravka, 6: Made a good save to deny Koumas early on but was well beaten on the three Liverpool goals.

Archie Gray , 5: One of Tottenham's better performers in the first half but allowed Gakpo onto his right foot far too easily.

Tosin Adarabioyo , 5: Looks to be Tottenham's fourth-choice centre-back and hardly suggested he deserves to be any higher.

Marcos Senesi , 4: Caught out on the ball on a couple of occasions when playing out from the back.

Destiny Udogie , 5: Showed up well in his battle with Ngumoha and offered a couple of moments from threat from left back.

Rodrigo Bentancur , 4: Looked slow on the ball and off the pace. Blitzed by Liverpool's young midfielders at times.

Lucas Bergvall, 6: Produced a couple of bursts forward but spurned a brilliant chance to open the scoring.

Mohammed Kudus , 6: Wasted a glorious chance to equalise from under the crossbar but brought some flashes on his first start of the season.

Conor Gallagher, 4: Scored Tottenham's first goal of the season, at long last, but he was wasteful on the ball at times and guilty of some loose touches in midfield.

Mathys Tel, 5: Crafted a couple of opportunities for others on the left wing, but brought off in the second half without having made enough impact.

Omar Marmoush, 6: Similarly, had bright moments. Struggled leading the line but then was denied by an excellent Mamardashvili after fashioning a chance for himself coming off the left.

Andy Robertsons, 6: Came on to an excellent reception on his Anfield return.

Matheus Fernandes , 7: Tottenham improved when he was added to the midfield.

James Maddison , 7: Made a real difference when brought on to No 10.

Savio, 5: Flashed a glorious late chance wide of the post.

articles.title: 5 major silver linings from the Chargers' Week 1 loss to the Cardinals
articles.summary: Don't panic over the final score from the loss to the Cardinals. The film shows several bright spots for the Chargers.
articles.body:
While the Chargers suffered a frustrating 26-14 season-opening loss to the Cardinals , several things provided strong building blocks for the rest of the season.

Here are five silver linings from the Week 1 game.

The most important development for the Chargers ' long-term outlook occurred along the offensive line. Tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt both made their highly anticipated returns, played the entire game, and left the contest completely healthy. Slater allowed just two pressures, while Alt allowed none on 39 pass-blocking snaps. Last season's injury-riddled campaign severely handcuffed the offense. With both cornerstone blockers back, quarterback Justin Herbert has the edge protection he needs.

Ladd McConkey 's return to rookie season form

Any questions about who would serve as the focal point of the passing attack were answered. McConkey looked like his highly productive 2024 rookie self, leading all Chargers pass-catchers with five receptions for 82 yards. He was spectacular on the team's opening drive, hauling in three catches for 60 yards to get the offense humming. McConkey later kept the Bolts within striking distance with an incredibly athletic eight-yard touchdown catch in the corner of the end zone in the third quarter. He is day-to-day with a rib injury, and it's unclear if he will play this weekend against the Raiders . But it's clear the chemistry between him and Herbert is as strong as ever.

No one knew who would emerge as the top pass-catching tight end, but it was Njoku who stepped up in the first game. He led the group in every receiving category, catching all five of his targets for 58 yards while also running the most routes (17) of any Chargers tight end. Oronde Gadsden II was efficient in a smaller role (2-for-2, 32 yards), and Charlie Kolar ran a solid number of routes (12) but wasn't targeted in the passing game that week. Njoku's ability to get open and create yards after the catch gave the Chargers another much-needed spark in a rather underwhelming offense on Sunday. It'll be worth monitoring the tight end target share as the weeks go on.

With veteran center Tyler Biadasz suffering a season-ending injury, Slaughter, the second-round pick, was thrown straight into the fire for his first career regular-season start. The 23-year-old experienced some lows, logging two costly penalties during a sequence late in the fourth quarter that ultimately left the offense stranded in a third-and-30 situation. But the former Florida product held his own in pass protection for most of the game, allowing zero pressures against a solid Cardinals interior.

Despite the overall defensive struggles, coach Mike Elston's group played well. They contained the Cardinals' rushing attack, ultimately limiting them to 3.4 yards per carry. Teair Tart 's ability to absorb double teams and clog running lanes earned him a 70.3 PFF grade, making him one of the Chargers' top five defensive performers for the game. Building off his active rookie campaign, Jamaree Caldwell was also highly active. He recorded five tackles and broke through for a quarterback hit on Jacoby Brissett .

articles.title: Harry Brook's brilliant 114 not out leads England to dominant T20 win over Sri Lanka
articles.summary: England piled up 254-4 after being put into bat in Southampton and that was mainly down to Brook, who has now scored 288 runs without getting out in the T20...
articles.body:
SOUTHAMPTON, England (AP) — England captain Harry Brook smashed 10 fours and six sixes in an unbeaten 114 off just 49 balls to set up a dominant 119-run win over Sri Lanka on Tuesday in the first of their three T20 internationals.

England piled up 254-4 after being put into bat in Southampton and that was mainly down to Brook, who has now scored 288 runs without getting out in the T20 format after unbeaten innings of 79 and 95 against India in July.

Opener Jos Buttler also weighed in with 80 off 44 balls for England.

The Sri Lankans attempted the second-highest chase in the history of T20 internationals and didn't get close. They were dismissed for 135, with Dunith Wellalage top-scoring with 33 and Sonny Baker having figures of 3-12 off his four overs.

There will be three ODIs between the teams after the T20 series, which continues on Thursday with the second match in Cardiff.

articles.title: Lusty at the double as Larne sink Cliftonville
articles.summary: Larne make it consecutive 2-0 wins with a routine victory over Cliftonville at Inver Park as Matty Lusty scored both goals.
articles.body:
Larne made it consecutive 2-0 wins with a routine victory over Cliftonville at Inver Park as Matty Lusty scored both goals.

Larne bossed the opening hour of the affair, and they really should have been home and dry by 30 minutes.

Lusty scored twice in a frenetic first half and the Invermen then squandered multiple chances in the second half to extend their lead, with Reds goalkeeper PJ Morrison pulling off a number of impressive stops.

The victory maintains Larne's unbeaten start to the season and moves Gary Haveron's men up to third in the table.

Larne started the brighter of the two sides with captain Tomas Cosgrove causing havoc down the right.

On seven minutes he zipped in a cross from the right and Lusty almost poked it home at the near post, but Cliftonville turned it behind.

Then, six minutes later, the hosts made the breakthrough. Cosgrove again provided from the right, and this time Lusty took the ball on the edge of the area before seeing his deflected effort fly past Morrison.

Cliftonville had to wait until almost the half-hour mark for their first chance. Liam McStravick picked up the ball on the edge of the Larne area and let fly with a low drive that had Rohan Ferguson nervous, but it flashed just wide of the left-hand upright.

Paul O'Neill then went close twice for Larne before Lusty eventually did grab a second on 38 minutes.

The striker then embarked on a mazy run into the Cliftonville area before he shot into the left-hand side of the goal.

Just after the break a mistake at the back almost let McStravick in on goal but his shot was superbly blocked by a lunging Matthew Ridley.

On the hour mark Ridley brought the best of Morrison once more with a powerful header but the goalkeeper made a tremendous reaction save to keep his team.

Morrison almost undid his good work minutes later when he was robbed with the ball at his feet by O'Neill, with the ball rolling to Lusty who shot from 20 yards but Morrison made amends with another superb diving save.

Larne manager Gary Haveron: "The boys worked incredibly, incredibly hard.

"To play the football that they played in the first half, they were excellent. We came out so fast and we got after them nicely.

"We missed some big chances but their keeper pulled off some absolutely unbelievable saves and the only criticism is that we should have been out of sight by half-time."

articles.title: Paul George Addresses Celtics Fans' Pushback After Sixers Trade
articles.summary: Former 76ers forward, Paul George discussed his unpopular trade to the Boston Celtics during his introductory news conference
articles.body:
Paul George 's two-season tenure with the Philadelphia 76ers came to an abrupt end earlier this summer, when he was traded to the Boston Celtics as part of the deal that brought Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia . George's time with the Sixers was marred by injuries; however, he came up big for Nick Nurse's team during the opening round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs, helping the Sixers bounce back from 3-1 down to eliminate Boston.

On Tuesday, September 15, George addressed the Boston media during his introductory news conference . Among a range of questions, George provided well-thought-out answers when asked about the controversial circumstances that led to his landing in Boston and how he felt about the fans' lukewarm reaction to his addition.

"Listen, I understand the circumstances," George said. "I understand how huge JB was not only for the organization, but here in the city...To be honest, it's (the pushback on his arrival) fair."

While George is already preparing for his first season in Celtics green, Sixers fans are gearing up for a potential championship season. Not only did the franchise acquire Brown this summer, but they also landed LeBron James in free agency, giving themselves a legitimate super team and a genuine shot at a title run.

In George's two seasons with the Sixers, he averaged 16.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, 4 assists, and 1.8 steals per game, suiting up for 78 regular-season contests. He shot 37.5 percent from deep and 48.9 percent from the two-point range. Although his time in Philadelphia didn't lead to a championship run, his tenure ultimately helped lead to the acquisition of Brown, and for that, Sixers fans will undoubtedly be grateful.

articles.title: What the Bills first injury report of the week really tells us.
articles.summary: Buffalo didn’t actually practice Monday, but the short week means the Bills still had to estimate who would — and wouldn’t — have participated.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills returned from their little field trip to Houston fairly healthy , but now as they prepare to face the Detroit Lions on Thursday Night Football's Week 2 airing, they aren't going to have much time to heal up what things bumps and bruises they are dealing with.

The first report of Week 2 is a little longer than last week's, but it's still not scary.

NOTE: This tracker will be updated following each injury report leading up to kickoff.

_____________________________________________________________________________

It's important to remember that the Bills did not actually practice on Monday. This list just represents what they estimate participation would have been had they actually done anything much more than film work and rest and recovery exercises.

The good news is that DJ Moore 's quick trip to the medical tent Sunday afternoon, along with Josh Allen 's temporary hand discomfort, didn't amount to anything.

I would expect Ty Johnson to return this week, but if he does, what does that mean for Frank Gore , Jr.? The second-year running back was called up from the practice squad Sunday and out snapped Ray Davis on offense. In fact, the Bills' fourth running back doubled Davis's snaps: Gore, Jr. 10, Davis 5. Offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael, Jr. — or Joe Brady depending on how we want to look at the Buffalo offense – seemed very content using Gore, Jr. in a blocking role.

It's unlikely that Bernard will be unavailable, but if he can't we could see Shaq Thompson called up from the practice squad.

Bishop was technically "downgraded" to limited after an estimated full practice on Monday. There's no serious indication he could miss this game, however. Apparently Sanders was sick, which led to his absence. He did not play in Week 1 against the Texans, remember.

I'm mostly zeroing in on Johnson. Despite getting in a practice on Friday before Week 1's game in Houston, Buffalo decided to keep the veteran on the sidelines as he nurses his hamstring injury back to full health. For as much as it might seem like he should be close to 100% by now — after suffering the injury in the Blue & Red Scrimmage in early August — the Bills could be staring at the 10-day layoff after this game and decide to keep him on the shelf for one more (game) week.

Fortunately, DJ Moore did not find himself on the official injury report after this update from Syracuse.com's Matt Parrino:

It appears all is well for Moore two days before this Week 2 showdown with Detroit in prime time.

Miller and Scruggs are the blockers to monitor on this short week for the Lions. The former was the club's first-round pick out of Clemson and played 77 snaps in Week 1. Only allowed one pressure. Scruggs is Detroit's starting center, and he also played on all 77 offensive snaps for Detroit in their Week 1 victory.

If Miller can't go, veteran Larry Borom is the Lions swing tackle. He's appeared in 64 games with 38 starts in his six seasons to date.

As for Scruggs, who, at this point, seems more likely to play than Miller, if he's unavailable for Thursday night's game, the Lions would have to do some positional shuffling, as they don't have a dedicated backup center on the 53-man roster right now.

It's now trending in the direction of the Lions being down both their starting left guard — Mahogany — and first-round pick right tackle — Miller in this game. As would be the case for any team, not having those two starters up front would be rather sizable losses for the Lions in this one. I wonder how much the short week plays in here.

The only other notable development from Tuesday's report is the sudden inclusion of Reed, the veteran (former Jets ) cornerback with a foot injury.
